item.title: Hashigui-iwa: The Bridge-Pillar Rocks of Kushimoto — Guide
item.description: Hashigui-iwa, on the coast at Kushimoto near the southern tip of Honshu, is one of Wakayama’s most striking natural sights: a line of roughly 40 rock pillars marching some 850 metres out into the sea toward Oshima island, looking uncannily like the surviving piers of a great bridge. Legend credits Kobo Daishi with attempting to build a bridge here in a single night; geology credits softer rock eroding away around harder intrusions.
